questions_and_answers.question_text: What is commonly omitted from a Chinese sentence when it is clear from the context?
How does Chinese compare with English in this respect?
In exchange 8, which word is missing from the reply Bú xìng Mǎ. Xìng Wáng.?
Write the Chinese for "Is your surname Fāng?"
Rewrite the reply in exchange 8 with the subject included.
What does the note tell you about the subject of a Chinese sentence?

answers.answer_text: It is quite common in Chinese — much commoner than in English — to omit the subject of a sentence when it is clear from the context.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Give the Chinese sentence meaning "My surname isn't Wáng."
Which verb is negated in exchanges 6, 7, and 8?
Why is bú, and not bù, used before xìng?

answers.answer_text: Because xìng is in the Falling tone, and bù becomes bú before a Falling tone.

questions_and_answers.question_text: What is the full English meaning of the reply Bú xìng Mǎ. Xìng Wáng.?

articles.text:
6. A: Nǐ xìng Fāng ma?                      Is your surname Fāng?
   B: Wǒ bú xìng Fāng.                      My surname isn't Fāng.

7. A: Wǒ xìng Wáng.                         My surname is Wáng.
   B: Wǒ bú xìng Wáng.                      My surname isn't Wáng.

8. A: Nǐ xìng Mǎ ma?                        Is your surname Mǎ?
   B: Bú xìng Mǎ. Xìng Wáng.                My surname isn't Mǎ. It's Wáng.

Note on No. 8

It is quite common in Chinese--much commoner than in English--to omit the subject of a sentence when it is clear from the context.
